**Stable, published under the npm `latest` dist-tag.** A plain
`npx @candid-core/cli` runs this version once it is published; `beta` stays on
0.2.0-beta.1. Until 1.0, any release may change the CLI grammar, the library
API, and the request/response shapes. Pin an exact version.

`@candid-core/schema` 0.3 breaks the 0.2 API (principal values are canonical text, collapsing opts are boxed, every `vec nat8` is a `Uint8Array`, generated modules use a new binding layout and may omit declarations, and the `./actor`, `./transport-icp`, `./forms` and `./labels` subpaths are gone); there is no compatibility layer.

## Installation

```sh
npm install --save-exact @candid-core/schema@0.3.0
npm install --save-dev --save-exact @candid-core/cli@0.2.0
npx @candid-core/cli@0.2.0 gen ./service.did -o ./generated
```

## Pairing

- **Peer**: `@candid-core/schema` at exactly `0.3.0` (optional, as before;
  `^0.2.0` in 0.1.0, exactly `0.3.0-beta.1` in 0.2.0-beta.1). The emitted
  modules need that release's `Principal` export and boxed options, and the
  generator and that release's `schemaFromContract` agree on blobs and
  omissions only within one release. The schema release is published first.
- **Embedded revision**: `candid-core` 0.1.0-beta.3 and the `candid-core-ts`
  generator, both compiled from the commit the release is dispatched from (the
  run records the SHA). That commit's `candid-core` source is ahead of the
  crates.io 0.1.0-beta.3 archive by four changes not yet in a crate release:
  a `.did` source may begin with one UTF-8 byte order mark (#176, #177),
  which beta.3 refuses; a run of more than 256 consecutive comments is
  refused with `resource_limit_exceeded` (#219), which beta.3 compiles up to
  a stack-dependent length and then aborts on; a type on a cycle that passes
  only through `opt` is refused with `did_type_check_error` (#234), which
  beta.3 compiles; and the crate's Contract JSON loaders refuse a struct
  written as a JSON array (#235), which beta.3's accept. No input of this
  package reaches the last one: `gen`, `didToContract` and `didToModule`
  read `.did` sources and never load a Contract document. Inputs both accept
  produce the same Contract and identities, and the envelopes' `producer`
  still reads `0.1.0-beta.3`.

## Public API against 0.1.0

The previous stable release. Library (`lib/index.d.ts`, against 0.1.0's
`gitHead`, `33f2af2b604e0df0b5ed0b382063c574941e27c8`), comment-stripped
declaration text of every kept name compared. The rebuilt tarball's integrity
was not reproduced, because its wasm needs the release toolchain; instead,
every file of the registry's 0.1.0 tarball that carries the API
(`lib/index.d.ts`, `lib/index.js`, `bin/cli.js`, `package.json`), and its
`README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`, is byte-identical to that `gitHead`, and the
same holds for the registry's 0.2.0-beta.1 against its `gitHead`,
`a65d7e204135ef80a4802f07f1153bbefe913d8f`. That tarball's `lib/index.d.ts`,
`lib/index.js` and `bin/cli.js` are also byte-identical to this release's,
which is what "unchanged against 0.2.0-beta.1" below rests on.

| Name | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `didToModule` | signature unchanged; **BREAKING** behaviour: returns `{ ok: true, module, omitted }` for interfaces it used to refuse with `ts_generation_refused` |
| `ModuleSuccess` | **BREAKING** (type), gains a required `omitted: Omission[]` |
| `Omission` | added |
| `CliReport`, `CliEntryReport`, `CliEntryStatus` | added (the `--json` document) |
| `init`, `didToContract`, `Sources`, `SourceSpan`, `RelatedLocation`, `ResourceLimitInfo`, `Diagnostic`, `Failure`, `FieldNameTriple`, `ContractEnvelope` | unchanged |
| `peerDependencies` | **BREAKING**, `@candid-core/schema` `^0.2.0` becomes exactly `0.3.0` |

Command line:

| 0.1.0 | 0.2.0 |
| --- | --- |
| `candid-core-cli gen <service.did> [-o <dir>]` | `candid-core-cli gen <service.did>... [-o <dir>] [--json] [--check]` (additive) |
| exit 1 with `ts_generation_refused` for an unrepresentable declaration | **BREAKING**: exit 0, module written without it, one `warning: omitted …` line per omission on stderr |
| a `.did` with a run of 257 or more consecutive comments compiles up to a stack-dependent length (2 825 measured, Node 24.2, macOS arm64), then crashes with an uncaught `RangeError` | **BREAKING**: `resource_limit_exceeded` (`source_nesting`, limit 256, `observed` 257), exit 1 |
| a `.did` holding a type on a cycle through `opt` alone (`type T = opt T;`) is refused with `ts_generation_refused`, exit 1, because such a type wraps `opt` in `opt` (0.2.0-beta.1 generates it, boxed) | refused with `did_type_check_error` naming the type, exit 1, nothing written for that entry (**BREAKING** against 0.2.0-beta.1; against 0.1.0 the diagnostic's code and phase change) |
| `wrote <path>` for every output | `unchanged <path>` when the file already holds the bytes (not rewritten) |
| one entry | several; every entry attempted, exit 1 if any failed; duplicate stems are a usage error (64) |

Generated modules (the text this tool writes):

- **BREAKING**: `$`-prefixed local bindings under a namespace import,
  exported under the Candid names; names that collided with the module's own
  bindings, with globals, or with reserved words now generate.
- **BREAKING**: principals are `$.Principal` (was `$.PrincipalValue`).
- **BREAKING**: collapsing opts generate, boxed, where they were refused.
- **BREAKING**: a use of a declared primitive renders structurally, and every
  `vec nat8` is `Uint8Array`.
- **BREAKING**: unrepresentable declarations are omitted with their
  dependents, and listed in a `// Omitted:` header.
- `.did` doc comments become JSDoc; method parameters take the `.did`
  argument names.

Against 0.2.0-beta.1, `lib/index.d.ts`, `lib/index.js` and `bin/cli.js` are
unchanged, and so is every module `gen` writes for an input both accept; the
differences are the two refusals above, of a long comment run and of a type
on a cycle through `opt` alone. The embedded generator now
renders on an explicit stack and refuses a Contract with a cycle through no
declared node, which no `.did` source produces.

## Known limitations and deferred work

- The multi-entry bundle-root rule and the duplicate-stem refusal apply the
  issue's recommendations and may be revisited before 1.0 (#193).
- Two structurally equal record declarations still collapse to the first
  name (#197, "Not yet scheduled"), and declarations whose records
  canonicalize to one node share its field names: a named spelling beats a
  numeric one in any order, and of two names with one hash the one the
  provenance sidecar lists last wins (#229).
- The embedded `candid-core` is not byte-identical to any crates.io release
  (above); the next crate release carries all four changes, which the root
  changelog already records under `## Unreleased`.

## Irreversibility

An npm version number is permanent: once published it can be deprecated, but
never republished with other bytes. The wasm in the tarball is built in the
release job with the pinned release toolchain and `wasm-pack`, so its bytes
are those two pins applied to the dispatched commit.
